headline: India shrugs off Wall Street's AI rout as Bank Nifty hits a record

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Saturday, the twenty-first of November, and this is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most this weekend. First, India has broken away from a global sell-off. While Wall Street had its worst week since the pandemic on fears about artificial intelligence spending, the Sensex and Nifty closed Friday near nine-month highs, and Bank Nifty hit a fresh record.

Second, the rupee is heading for its best month in eight years. It crossed below 93 to the dollar on Friday, helped by foreign inflows and cheaper oil.

And third, a Reuters poll says the Reserve Bank is expected to raise interest rates in December, as inflation breaches its tolerance limit of 6 percent.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Let's start with how markets closed. The Sensex rose 1.08 percent on Friday to end at 83,919. The Nifty gained 1.12 percent to 25,800. It was a second straight day of gains, and a fourth straight weekly gain. For the week, the Sensex added 2.85 percent and the Nifty 2.61 percent. Over two days, the Sensex climbed close to 1,900 points.

Banks led the charge. Bank Nifty topped 64,000 for the first time and touched a record of around 64,600, up 2.5 percent on the day. IndusInd Bank jumped around 8 percent, near its 52-week high, after returning to quarterly profit. HDFC Bank hit an eight-month high and regained a market value of 13 lakh crore rupees. It is up 22 percent in November alone. State-run lenders such as SBI, Punjab National Bank and Canara Bank have rallied by up to 27 percent this month.

Hospitals were the other bright spot, with Apollo Hospitals and Max Healthcare the top Nifty gainers. Textile stocks hit a new high, with Indo Count and Welspun Living up as much as 8 percent. On the other side, Titan, Tata Steel and NTPC were the biggest losers, and metal and consumer durable stocks stayed under pressure. Vedanta fell over 3 percent after Citi cut its target price, citing weak zinc demand. Stocks linked to artificial intelligence, such as E2E Networks and Hitachi Energy India, fell up to 5 percent.

Volatility rose too, with India VIX up around 9 percent to above 17. Analysts told Business Standard that foreign institutional investors are buying so steadily that the bulls remain in control.

The levels to watch. Market experts expect the Nifty to head towards 26,000 next week. A move above that brings the record high of 26,373, from the fifth of January, into view. For Bank Nifty, one analyst sees support at 63,500 and resistance around 65,000.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
Now to IPOs and deals. The big story is Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, which listed on Nasdaq on Thursday after a record IPO of 93.5 billion dollars. Priced at 83 dollars, the shares closed 17 percent higher on day one. But on Friday they fell around 9 to 10 percent, nearly erasing the debut gain as the AI trade unravelled. Indian investors piled in. On debut day, Anthropic made up 40 percent of international investments on INDmoney and 11 percent of traded value on Vested.

Closer home, SEBI has cleared IPOs from Pristine Logistics and Infraprojects, and from Arohan Financial Services. NSE shares hit a record of 2,251 rupees, about 25 percent above their September IPO price. That makes NSE the world's fifth-largest listed exchange operator, ahead of Nasdaq and Hong Kong Exchanges. JM Financial sees NSE as a strong candidate for the MSCI India index, with a decision expected in February.

In stake sales, TPG-backed Newquest sold Shadowfax shares worth 115 crore rupees, cutting its holding to around 6 percent. And one index change for your calendar: Shriram Finance will replace Trent in the Sensex from the twenty-first of December.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script: A short results roundup. IndusInd Bank's September quarter showed a return to profit, stronger core income and better asset quality, though its margins narrowed. Across state-run banks, net profit hit a record 1.09 lakh crore rupees in the first half of this financial year, and their capital adequacy improved to 16.89 percent. In cement, a Moneycontrol analysis shows profit per tonne has dropped to its lowest level since early 2025, with companies raising prices to offset higher costs.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now to the economy and policy. A Reuters poll shows economists expect the Reserve Bank to raise the repo rate by a quarter point to 5.75 percent in December, and to 6 percent in February. Higher energy costs and an uneven monsoon are pushing prices up.

The rupee touched 92.91 to the dollar on Friday, a seven-month high. That's a gain of about 40 paise on the day and over a rupee this week, making it the best performing Asian currency in November. Chief Economic Adviser V Anantha Nageswaran said India may have to manage rupee strength, not weakness, next financial year, with several agencies expecting Brent crude below 80 dollars. Forex reserves, though, fell 14.21 billion dollars to 705.34 billion in the week to the thirteenth of November, mainly because of revaluation.

Core sector output grew 10.9 percent in October, a 31-month high, led by coal, electricity, iron ore and cement. On the farm side, the area under wheat is set for its steepest fall in 26 years, as farmers switch to chickpeas and rapeseed after weak rains.

SEBI was busy. It proposed scrapping the extra ownership disclosures for certain foreign portfolio investors, calling them out of step with global practice, and wants onboarding done in five business days. It also proposed an overall 12-year tenure cap for managing directors of exchanges and clearing corporations, and a lower age limit of 70 for public interest directors. Comments are due by the eleventh of December. Regulators are also studying dual-class shares for listings in India and GIFT City.

On tax, the Mumbai bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal stayed a demand of 8,520 crore rupees on the Singapore government, over gains made through its fund GIC. And Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman held her eighth and ninth pre-Budget meetings, with labour, housing and urban development stakeholders. The Budget is due on the first of February. Among the wish lists, the brokers' body ANMI wants securities transaction tax scrapped on delivery trades.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, it was a rough week on Wall Street. The Nasdaq 100 lost 5.6 percent and posted its worst week since March 2020. The S&P 500 fell for a seventh straight day, its longest losing streak since 2020, and slipped below its 200-day average. US markets lost about 6 trillion dollars in value in a week. Nvidia sank 14 percent after Reuters reported US regulators are looking into its accounting. AMD fell 7.7 percent after a short seller alleged China supply links, which AMD rejected. A hawkish Federal Reserve, signalling more rate hikes, added to the pressure.

Oil is heading for a third straight weekly fall, as shipments through the Strait of Hormuz recover. Mirae Asset Sharekhan sees Brent at 75 to 85 dollars next year. Gold had its worst week since March. And Bitcoin is near 61,000 dollars, down about a fifth since the end of October.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Now to your money. The Income Tax Department has issued FAQs on FAST-DS, the one-time scheme to disclose foreign assets, which closes on the thirty-first of December. If you hold a foreign bank account with up to 20 lakh rupees from disclosed sources, you don't need to file a declaration. Joint holders must disclose separately. The FAQs also cover a fee of 1 lakh rupees for one category, a 20 percent tolerance on property valuation, and immunity for partial disclosures.

Two tribunal rulings are worth noting. The Hyderabad bench deleted an addition of about 16 lakh rupees, after a taxpayer relied on CBDT limits for family jewellery found during a search. And the Jaipur bench rejected a capital loss of 20.67 lakh rupees on the sale of a Mercedes, ruling that a personally used car is not a capital asset, even if it is shown in the balance sheet.

On gold, the jewellers' body GJC has alerted the Bureau of Indian Standards about reports of rhenium and iridium alloys being used to add weight without adding purity. It says there is no reason to panic, but urges buyers to report suspected adulteration. Gold futures fell 4 percent on Friday to around one lakh twenty-three thousand rupees per 10 grams, and silver dropped 6 percent.

One more warning. SBI has alerted pensioners to fake messages asking them to update their pension payment order. Don't click such links or share your details. And the Reserve Bank has clarified which service exporters must file the export declaration form under the new foreign exchange rules.

That's the week. Markets are shut for the weekend. Next week, watch whether the Nifty can clear 26,000, how Wall Street handles the AI sell-off, and US growth and jobs data, along with manufacturing numbers from major economies. Two dates for your calendar: the eleventh of December for SEBI's consultations, and the thirty-first for the FAST-DS deadline. Have a lovely weekend.
